reading.body:
A founding OpenAI CTO launched Thinking Machines Lab in February 2025 to build collaborative, multimodal AI systems that work with people rather than pursuing full autonomy.

Murati's departure from OpenAI after nearly six years, including a stint as interim CEO during the November 2023 board crisis, marked a shift in focus within the AI leadership class. Her new company's stated philosophy centers on human-AI collaboration rather than systems designed for independent operation. This represents a distinct position in the market at a time when debate over AI autonomy remains unresolved.

The company's emphasis on multimodal systems and collaboration means Thinking Machines Lab operates in a narrower technical scope than the large-scale model training that dominates compute infrastructure discussion. The data provided does not specify the company's compute requirements, funding, facilities, or power consumption, making it impossible to assess how its technical approach translates to infrastructure demands. What the company prioritizes and how those priorities affect resource intensity remain separate questions.

standing.watch: What remains unresolved in the records is the fate of the OpenAI cases, all of which are marked as filed with docket monitoring active and no development recorded yet by this tracker, including those with dates such as Bass v. OpenAI, LLC on 2026-09-28, United States v. OpenAI OpCo LLC on 2026-09-21, GRANT v. OPENAI INC on 2026-09-30, Smigelski v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC on 2026-09-17, and JIANG v. OPENAI GROUP PBC on 2026-09-23. The records also leave open the trajectory of Thinking Machines Lab, which launched publicly on February 18, 2025, with funding and valuation fields left blank. No pending case names Murati directly, and the records do not indicate any planned listing or dispute involving her or Thinking Machines Lab. Where the records are thin, they say less: the coverage of her new company is limited to its founding, launch date, and stated focus.
standing.record: The site's records tie Murati to two companies, OpenAI, where she is listed as an executive, and Thinking Machines Lab, which she founded in 2025. The lawsuits on the site name OpenAI entities rather than Murati personally, including USA Today Co., Inc. v. OpenAI Foundation, TradeSun, Inc. v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC, Bass v. OpenAI, LLC, United States v. OpenAI OpCo LLC, GRANT v. OPENAI INC, Smigelski v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC, and JIANG v. OPENAI GROUP PBC, all recorded as filed with docket monitoring active and no development recorded yet by this tracker. One further case, Buist v. Anthropic, PBC, names a different company and does not involve OpenAI. The pattern running through the records is a cluster of filed but undeveloped cases against OpenAI entities, alongside Murati's own move from an executive role there to founding and leading a separate AI company.
standing.standing: Mira Murati stands as the founder and CEO of Thinking Machines Lab, a public benefit corporation she founded in 2025 and launched publicly on February 18, 2025, focused on collaborative, multimodal AI systems. She also appears in the records as an executive of OpenAI, the San Francisco startup founded in 2015, where she became Chief Technology Officer in May 2022 and briefly served as interim CEO starting November 17, 2023, during the board crisis following Sam Altman's departure. Her departure from OpenAI was announced on September 25, 2024, after nearly six years at the company. The records show her influence spanning both an established AI lab and a newly launched venture she controls as CEO.
